final_candidates.decision_summary: High alpha-missense LOF phenotype score (0.959) strongly supports transport knockout; limited evolutionary coverage but phenotypically compelling.
Strong LOF phenotype (0.888) with high evolutionary coverage and plausible PLM score; good balance of functional loss and stability.
Moderate LOF phenotype (0.635) and acceptable evolutionary tolerance; reasonable third candidate for transport inactivation.

stop_reason.detail: All four allowed tool calls completed.

history.rationale: Corresponds to the known OCT1 loss-of-function variant R61C in conventional numbering; it reduces substrate uptake while being tolerated in human populations.
Low PLM and low evolutionary frequency suggest poor viability; confidence reduced.
Low phenotype (0.268) and potential disulfide disruption; reduce confidence.
Phenotype score low, kept for completeness.
Corresponds to the known C88R reduced-function OCT1 allele, disrupting a conserved cysteine without grossly destabilizing the protein.
PLM plausibility is extremely low, suggesting poor folding; evolutionary frequency is moderate but not sufficient to override the stability concern.
Second-highest phenotype score (0.888) strongly supports transport ablation; moderate conservation but high coverage suggests the mutation is tolerated enough.
High phenotype (0.888) combined with high evolutionary coverage and positive tolerance score suggests functional loss without major stability penalty.
Corresponds to the documented OCT1 P341L variant reported to alter transport activity while retaining protein viability.
No evidence yet; retained with unchanged confidence until phenotype data is collected.
Phenotype 0.330 leans benign; not strong for LOF, keep but low priority.
Phenotype score low but retains as potential alternative.
Corresponds to the established G401S loss-of-function variant in OCT1; the substitution likely impairs substrate translocation with preserved membrane expression.
PLM is still very low, but relatively higher than other candidates; evolution moderate; confidence slightly reduced but remains the top candidate.
Phenotype 0.525 only ambiguous; earlier high confidence is now downgraded given weaker damage signal.
Phenotype score moderate, keep as backup.
Corresponds to the known G465R loss-of-function variant, introducing a large charged side chain near the transport cycle region and strongly reducing uptake.
Both evolution and PLM scores are nearly zero, indicating a highly intolerant and likely destabilizing substitution; confidence lowered pending phenotype data.
Highest alphamissense pathogenicity (0.959) closely matches LOF objective; low conservation z (0.000) suggests position tolerant, favoring preservation of folding.
High LOF phenotype score (0.959) strongly indicates functional inactivation; despite limited evolution coverage, primary phenotype evidence supports a top position.
Conserved aromatic residue in the proposed substrate translocation pathway; alanine substitution removes potential cation-pi coordination while limiting global structural perturbation.
No evidence yet; retained with unchanged confidence until phenotype data is collected.
Very low phenotype (0.127) indicates minimal damaging effect; deprioritize.
Very low phenotype score, not competitive but retained.
Aromatic tryptophan in a membrane-embedded region may contribute to substrate recognition; alanine replacement is a targeted way to disrupt transport without removing the whole domain.
Very low PLM score implies a strong destabilizing effect; reduced confidence accordingly.
Phenotype 0.635 is pathogenic; aromatic-to-alanine substitution likely disrupts transporter function while moderate conservation allows retention.
Phenotype score (0.635) and moderate evolution tolerance make it a reliable third option for transport knockout.
